text:
rachael: heads up — saw a 2-3x p99 spike on long-context chat routes after the kernel-selector change rolled to staging. looks tied to increased eviction churn and sustained KV memory growth. repro on a few boxes. anyone digging?

sam: saw that too in graphs this morning. p50 fine, tail blows up. allocation trace shows reuse rate dropping.

alex: quick hypothesis — the new kernel selection introduces an extra memcpy for slab-aligned buffers on certain sequence lengths. that delays token emission and keeps KV pages hot longer, triggering FIFO fallthrough spikes.

maria: interesting — i ran a microbench with a 32k long context replay workload and got similar pattern. FIFO mode flips more frequently under this pattern vs LRU.

rachael: posting profiler snapshot from one repro run:
```
hotspots (sampled):
  memcpy_align_pad         34%
  kv_evict_scheduler       22%
  kernel_selector          18%
  async_writeback          9%
  lock_contention         7%
  other                   10%
```

alex: that memcpy_align_pad is the suspicious bit — it only shows up when we choose the AVX2-packed kernel path vs the small-block kernel. kernel_selector seems to prefer packed kernels for mid-length batches which misalign on our slab boundaries.

sam: log excerpt where eviction bursts start:
```
[12:03:21] route=chat-long ctx=31245 mem_used=78% kv_reuse=0.12 evicter_mode=FIFO
[12:03:22] kv_evict:start items=420 lanes=4
[12:03:22] kernel_select: packed_avx2 seq=128 buf_align=7 -> copy_needed
[12:03:23] token_emit delay=38ms p99
```

maria: repro steps I used: `./bench --route chat-long --seq 32k --batch-dist skewed --concurrency 6 --evict-policy auto` (commit 9f3b2c7). Results: p99 x2.7 and KV resident set increases steadily until recycle window.

rachael: ops-bot ran a staging deploy at 2024-10-09T10:00Z with that commit (deploy ID deploy-2201). Deploy logs show increased GC/evict events right after rollout.

ops-bot: FYI @rachael @sam @alex — flagged 5 hosts for deeper heap+perf traces. collecting perf.data and heap dumps now.

alex: quick experiment idea: force kernel_selector to prefer small-block kernel for sequences >= 64k or when slab fragmentation > 12% and see if eviction churn reduces. also try forcing LRU-only policy to test whether FIFO toggling is the main amplifier.

sam: i can run an A/B on 2 staging shards: one with `--evict-policy lru` and one with `--kernel-force small`. will share traces.

maria: also adding a micro-observability metric: `kv.reuse_rate_by_align` to check alignment correlation with reuse.

rachael: steps for follow-up:
- sam: run the A/B and upload perf traces to /tmp/repro-1719804321 (small files ok)
- alex: add a quick toggle to kernel_selector binary for local test (no heavy perf impact)
- maria: add the observability metric and run bench again
- ops-bot: keep collecting heap/kv telemetry for the flagged hosts

rachael: if this hypothesis holds, the real fix might be kernel_selector + allocator alignment cooperation (avoid copies) or making eviction policy de-prioritize transient misalignment churn. either way we should mitigate with LRU fallback before rollout. :warning:

sam: agreed. i'll start the A/B now and paste the perf links once uploaded.

deploy-bot: Deployment deploy-2201 rolled back on shard-3 at 2024-10-09T10:15Z due to elevated p99.

rachael: thanks. will coordinate a postmortem branch if we confirm root cause. keeping this thread as the single place for notes. :mag:
